content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Write a brief message with greeting, reason, detail, and closing. Model: “Hi An, I am late because the bus is slow. See you at the cafe. Minh” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use a short message clearly and politely. One useful response is: “Hi An, I am late because the bus is slow. See you at the cafe. Minh” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where a short message is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

language_focus: Write a brief message with greeting, reason, detail, and closing.
objectives: Write a brief message with greeting, reason, detail, and closing.
Use everyday written notes in one short, clear everyday exchange.

constraints: Do not reveal the transcript before the learner answers.
Ask exactly one comprehension question before showing the transcript.
Use only the supplied project-authored transcript.
listening.goal: Understand one clear detail in a short exchange about a short message.
listening.instruction: Listen once without reading to a short exchange about a short message. Answer the question, then ask to see the transcript and listen again.
listening.question: Why is Minh late?
listening.transcript: Hi Mai, I am late because the bus is slow. Please start without me. Minh

constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is available.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when no audio is supplied.
Give one observable sound, stress, or rhythm point rather than general pronunciation advice.
pronunciation.goal: Produce the identified sound, stress, or rhythm feature clearly in a useful phrase.
pronunciation.instruction: Read the concrete sound target aloud: Read the message in groups: HI MAI | I AM LATE | SEE YOU. Then read one lesson sentence slowly and once at normal speed.
pronunciation.target: Read the message in groups: HI MAI | I AM LATE | SEE YOU.

constraints: Give the tutor one role and the learner one role before the first turn.
Create an information gap: the tutor asks for one missing personal or practical detail.
Use no more than three tutor turns and give one correction only if it blocks meaning.
Finish after the learner has used the target and responded to one follow-up.
speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about a short message.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using a short message; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise a short message?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: Hi An, I am late because the bus is slow. See you at the cafe. Minh

constraints: Wait for the learner draft before feedback.
Give at most two brief improvement points about meaning, word order, or target use.
Do not replace the learner draft with a complete rewritten answer.
writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about a short message with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about a short message. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: Hi An, I am late because the bus is slow. See you at the cafe. Minh Submit your draft first.
